case_name: E-commerce missing canonical + JSON-LD + security headers

fixes.fix_explanation: A canonical tag tells search engines this is the authoritative URL for the page, preventing duplicate-content issues if the page is accessible via multiple URLs (e.g., with query strings or trailing slashes).
fixes.fix_location: Inside the <head> element, after the existing <meta name="description"> tag.

fixes.fix_code:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "Widget Pro",
  "description": "The Widget Pro is our flagship product. Built with precision engineering and available in 5 colors. Free shipping on orders over $50.",
  "image": "https://shop.example.com/images/widget-pro.jpg",
  "url": "https://shop.example.com/products/widget-pro",
  "brand": {
    "@type": "Brand",
    "name": "Example Shop"
  },
  "offers": {
    "@type": "Offer",
    "url": "https://shop.example.com/products/widget-pro",
    "priceCurrency": "USD",
    "availability": "https://schema.org/InStock",
    "seller": {
      "@type": "Organization",
      "name": "Example Shop",
      "url": "https://shop.example.com"
    }
  }
}
</script>
fixes.fix_explanation: JSON-LD structured data using the Product schema gives search engines rich, machine-readable information about the Widget Pro, making it eligible for Google rich results such as product panels and price snippets.
fixes.fix_location: Inside the <head> element, just before the closing </head> tag.

fixes.fix_explanation: This HTTP response header stops browsers from MIME-sniffing a response away from the declared content type, reducing the risk of drive-by download attacks and certain cross-site scripting vectors. Add it to your server configuration (e.g., nginx, Apache, or CDN/edge rules) so it is sent with every response.
fixes.fix_location: Server-level HTTP response header. For nginx add 'add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;' inside your server {} or location {} block. For Apache add 'Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"' in your .htaccess or VirtualHost config.

fixes.fix_explanation: The X-Frame-Options header prevents the page from being embedded in an <iframe> on a third-party domain, protecting users against clickjacking attacks. SAMEORIGIN allows framing only by pages on the same origin, which is appropriate for most e-commerce sites.
fixes.fix_location: Server-level HTTP response header. For nginx add 'add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;' inside your server {} or location {} block. For Apache add 'Header always set X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN"' in your .htaccess or VirtualHost config.
